messages:
devon (eng-runtime): heads up — FinEdge is pushing back on our SLA. They want p99 <= 250ms at sustained 50 qps for their private deployment. Product looped sales in.
sam (eng-ml): that's tight given their model (7B, long context). p95 target we can hit with microbatch=2 and kv cache, p99 is trickier (tail from occasional cache misses + kernel path).
lia (product): @devon can you summarize the options? sales needs a clear ask to the customer — what rollback/fallback looks like and any cost impact.
mike (sales): customer said they'll accept higher unit cost if we can guarantee p99 250ms. They prefer reserved capacity. Also asked if we can run a 2-week pilot.
devon (eng-runtime): short summary: options:
  1) enforce strict microbatch=1 (lower queueing latency) + aggressive KV sticky routing -> lower tail but throughput drops.
  2) microbatch=2 or 4 with fused kernels and dynamic kernel selection -> better throughput but p99 tail from cache churn.
  3) hybrid: canary route a subset to low-latency config, keep rest on cost-opt.
jen (eng-sre): can confirm we can carve a dedicated pool for pilot. Need to test steady 50 qps + spikes.
perf-bot: latest profiling run #2026-03-15: model=finedge-v1, seq=1024, qps=50, microbatch=2 -> p95 118ms, p99 312ms
sam (eng-ml): attaching quick perf breakdown (rough):
```
config      p95   p99   cpu/gpu notes
mb=1        125ms 260ms high gpu idle, kernel switch cost low
mb=2        118ms 312ms better gputil, cache miss tail up
mb=4        140ms 420ms highest throughput, worst tail
fused-kern  130ms 280ms fewer kernel switches, slightly better tail
``` 
devon (eng-runtime): root cause for p99 bump is KV cache eviction storms when multiple tenants hit similar prefixes -> cache misses cause full kv warm leading to heavy kernel work and thread contention.
lia (product): can we mitigate without changing customer infra? i.e., config knobs only.
sam (eng-ml): yes: increase KV sticky TTL, enable per-model small hot-cache prefetch, and prefer fused kernels on that model. Also tweak scheduler to avoid batching two large seqs together.
devon (eng-runtime): proposed experiment for pilot:
  - Dedicated pool (50 qps reserved)
  - microbatch=2, fused kernels enabled
  - KV TTL increased from 30s -> 300s for that pool
  - canary 10% traffic run for 48h with tail monitoring
mike (sales): if we do that, what are the expected p95/p99 numbers? customer asks for 250ms p99.
devon (eng-runtime): best-guess after changes: p95 ~120ms, p99 ~240-260ms depending on spike patterns. Not guaranteed until we run canary.
jen (eng-sre): I'll provision dedicated pool and start canary once devon pushes config. Need rollout doc + abort thresholds.
devon (eng-runtime): config snippet I'm going to apply:
```
pool: finedge-pilot
reserved_qps: 50
microbatch: 2
kernel_mode: fused
kv_cache_ttl_secs: 300
prefetch_hot_keys: true
abort_if_p99>300ms_for_10m: true
```
sam (eng-ml): also enabling lightweight tracing for tail traces (20ms sampling of 1/100 requests) so we can capture KV miss stack.
lia (product): sounds good. I will tell customer we can pilot for 2 weeks with the above config, and we target p99 250ms but will include a clause that if tail persists beyond thresholds we will propose dedicated optimizations (code/kernel work) and adjust pricing.
mike (sales): customer ok with pilot. they want weekly checkpoints.
devon (eng-runtime): next steps: I'll push config to canary by EOD, run 48h canary, post perf dashboard. jen will prepare rollback runbook. sam will collate traces.
perf-bot: canary scheduled: starts=1762348800, duration=172800s (48h)
devon (eng-runtime): noted. thanks team. :thumbsup:
